purpose: Every title-only item says why it is title-only (the fetch failed, the page had nothing to extract, a named content rule fired, or the model judged it not substantive), so the cause of failures is a query instead of an investigation, and the light model the daemon already pays for backs the code check up on junk the rules cannot see.
form:
One reason vocabulary, produced where each decision is made and combined in the one place title-only is decided.

1. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/readability.py` gains `readability_failure(content) -> str | None`, returning `empty`, `placeholder:rss_no_content`, `placeholder:reddit_link_only`, `placeholder:youtube_no_transcript`, `no_prose` or `js_wall` for the first check that fails and None for readable content; `is_readable(content)` becomes `readability_failure(content) is None`, so every current caller is unchanged.

2. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/article_extractor.py` `extract_article` (line 19) returns an `ArticleResult` dataclass of `text: str | None` and `outcome`, one of `extracted`, `empty` (fetched, trafilatura found nothing) and `fetch_failed`, with a `detail` string (the HTTP status trafilatura's `fetch_response` reports, or the exception class name). Its three callers (fetchers/rss.py, fetchers/reddit.py, refetch.py) read `.text` where they read the string today. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/fetchers/youtube.py` `_extract_transcript` (line 334) returns the same pair shape for transcripts (`fetch_failed` with yt-dlp's error, for example HTTP 429, versus `empty` for no subtitles). Each fetcher that attempted an extraction puts `{"outcome": ..., "detail": ...}` under `fetch_outcome` in the item's `analysis` beside `metrics`, which the orchestrator merge (orchestrator.py:697) already carries into storage.

3. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/summarizer.py`: the standard prompt's OUTPUT FORMAT (line 297, shared by standard, brief and detailed modes) and the diff prompt (line 386) gain one boolean field `substantive`, false when the content is not the piece itself (a JavaScript, cookie or bot-check notice, site navigation or footer text, an error or login page, a bare link, a teaser with no body) and true otherwise, including short genuine posts. `ContentSummary` gains `substantive: bool | None`; a reply without the field leaves it None rather than failing the parse or reading as false.

4. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/analysis.py` `build_llm_analysis` (line 52) takes the fetcher's `fetch_outcome` as an optional argument (orchestrator.py:168 passes it from the item; `analyze repair` at cli/src/cli/analyze.py:198 passes the stored one) and sets `title_only_reason` to the first that applies: `content:<rule>` from `readability_failure`, prefixed `fetch_failed:<detail>; ` when the fetch outcome was `fetch_failed`; else `model:not_substantive` when `substantive` is False; else None. `title_only` is `title_only_reason is not None`.

5. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/storage.py` `get_readable_external_ids` (lines 688-691) also treats rows whose `analysis.title_only_reason` starts with `model:` as settled, so a model-only title-only item is not re-extracted and re-analysed every cycle. `LIST_ANALYSIS_KEYS` gains `title_only_reason`. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/api.py` mirrors it top-level beside `_item_title_only`, and `ContentItemModel` in api_models.py gains `title_only_reason: str | None = None`.

6. `cli/src/cli/list.py` marks title-only rows (lowercase 'title only', like the TUI and web) and `cli/src/cli/get.py` prints 'Title only: <reason>'; `--json` output carries both fields through as the API returns them.

7. `docs/architecture/boundaries.md` title-only contract (line 55) adds: the item stores `title_only_reason` from the fixed vocabulary above, and the light model's `substantive` verdict is one input to the decision.

8. Tests: `readability_failure` returns each reason for its fixture and None for the readable ones; `extract_article` against a local HTTP server returns `fetch_failed` with the status for a 429 and a 404, `empty` for a page with no extractable text and `extracted` for an article; the summarizer parses `substantive` true, false and absent (None) from a stub LLM server at the real HTTP boundary; `build_llm_analysis` yields each reason and none for a readable, substantive item; the retry query skips a `model:` row and keeps retrying a `content:` row; the CLI list and get render the marker and reason. Each new test is shown red with its behavior removed.
commitments: Every title-only item stores `title_only_reason` from one fixed vocabulary: `content:<rule>` (optionally prefixed `fetch_failed:<detail>; `) or `model:not_substantive`.
`extract_article` and the YouTube transcript extraction report fetch failure, empty extraction and success as three different outcomes, and fetchers store that outcome on the item.
The light summarize call returns a `substantive` boolean in its existing JSON; no LLM call is added, and an absent field is unknown, not false.
Title-only is decided only in `build_llm_analysis`: code check fails, or the model says not substantive.
A model-only title-only item is not retried each fetch cycle.
`is_readable` keeps its boolean contract for every current caller.
The CLI shows the title-only marker and reason, matching the TUI and web marker.

Measured before design on cerebro, 2026-10-03, with the instruction this design adds: 50 of 51 known-junk items called not substantive; of 40 short and 10 long readable-by-code items, 5 short ones called not substantive, and all 5, opened, were junk the code missed (bare links, gibberish, an X page of view counts); none were real content.
sacrifices: Stored items keep no reason until re-analysed or refetched; the vocabulary applies to new analysis forward.
A real but unusual short post the model misjudges is labeled title-only and skips deep extraction; the measured sample had none.
The TUI and web show the marker but not the reason; the reason reaches them through the API, and of the three interfaces only the CLI prints it.
A model-only title-only item whose page later becomes substantive is not re-fetched by the retry loop; `prismis-daemon refetch` or `force_refetch` still re-processes it.
risk: If the model's verdict drifts (a model change or prompt edit) it can mark real content title-only, which shows as a rise in `model:not_substantive` reasons that is now a single query to see; if a fetcher misses recording its outcome, the reason falls back to the content rule alone, which is no worse than today.
